# Copilot Instructions — ACS Email Domain Checker

> **Purpose**: Guide GitHub Copilot (and developers) through the codebase structure so you know where to look, what each file does, and how the build pipeline works.

---

## Architecture Overview

This is a **single-file PowerShell web application** that runs a local HTTP server to check DNS records for Azure Communication Services email domain verification. The web UI is a Single Page Application (SPA) embedded directly inside the PowerShell script as a here-string.

### Runtime flow

1. **CLI mode** (`-TestDomain example.com`): runs DNS checks, outputs JSON, and exits.
2. **Server mode** (default): starts an HTTP listener, serves the SPA UI, and exposes routes such as `/`, `/index.html`, `/dns`, `/api/base`, `/api/mx`, `/api/records`, `/api/whois`, `/api/dmarc`, `/api/dkim`, `/api/cname`, `/api/reputation`, `/api/website`, `/api/nameservers`, `/api/propagation`, `/api/metrics`, `/api/auth/event`, `/terms`, and `/privacy`.

---

## Build System

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Build-Release.ps1` | Optionally refreshes local UI assets via `Download-UiAssets.ps1`, then concatenates all `src/*.ps1` files (sorted by numeric prefix + optional letter suffix) into the monolithic `acs-domain-checker.ps1`. |

### How to rebuild

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./Build-Release.ps1 -Force
```

By default, `Build-Release.ps1` also invokes `Download-UiAssets.ps1` first so local Lucide and flag SVG assets are present under `assets/vendor/...`. Use `-SkipUiAssetDownload` when rebuilding in an offline or restricted environment.

> **Important:** The build uses a custom sort key (numeric prefix then optional letter suffix) instead of plain `Sort-Object Name`. PowerShell's default culture-sensitive string comparison treats hyphens as ignorable, which causes `20a-*` to sort before `20-*` and breaks the HTML assembly order.

The `acs-domain-checker.ps1` at the repo root is the **built artifact** — do **not**
edit it directly. All changes go into `src/` files, then rebuild.

### Quick validation

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./acs-domain-checker.ps1 -TestDomain example.com
```

---

## Source File Map (`src/`)

Files are numbered `NN-Name.ps1` to control concatenation order. The build sorts lexicographically, so `20a-*` sorts after `20-*` and before `21-*`.

### Script Header & Parameters

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `00-Header.ps1` | ~161 | Script-level `param()` block, parameter definitions (`-Port`, `-Bind`, `-TestDomain`, etc.), global variables, container detection |

### Domain Parsing & WHOIS

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `01-DomainParsing.ps1` | ~300 | `Get-RegistrableDomain`, `Get-ParentDomains` — extract registrable domain from FQDN. Registrable-domain resolution uses the official **Public Suffix List (PSL)** when available: `Get-PublicSuffixData` loads/parses a cached `public_suffix_list.dat` (path from `$env:ACS_PSL_FILE`, set in `00-Header.ps1`), only consulting the ICANN section so the result stays WHOIS-queryable (PRIVATE-domain suffixes like `blogspot.com` are skipped). The file is refreshed at build time by `Download-UiAssets.ps1` and lazily refreshed at runtime when missing or older than `ACS_PSL_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (default 30) unless `ACS_PSL_DISABLE_DOWNLOAD=1`. The parsed rule sets (exact/wildcard/exception) are cached in-process via `$script:PublicSuffixCache`, keyed by path + last-write time so a refresh re-parses. `Get-PublicSuffixFromLabels` implements the official PSL longest-match + exception + `*` default algorithm. When no PSL file can be loaded, `Get-RegistrableDomain` falls back to a small **inline** multi-label suffix list (kept inline, not in a `$script:` variable, so it works inside worker runspaces where only function definitions are copied). New PSL functions (`Get-PublicSuffixListPath`, `Update-PublicSuffixListFile`, `ConvertFrom-PublicSuffixListFile`, `Get-PublicSuffixData`, `Get-PublicSuffixFromLabels`) are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`. |
| `02-WhoisProviders.ps1` | ~614 | Three WHOIS backends: `Invoke-SysinternalsWhoisLookup` (Windows), `Invoke-LinuxWhoisLookup` (Linux), `Invoke-TcpWhoisLookup` (raw TCP fallback) |
| `04-RdapLookups.ps1` | ~225 | RDAP protocol lookups (`Invoke-RdapLookup`), plus WhoisXML and GoDaddy API fallbacks. `Invoke-WhoisXmlLookup` sends the API key in the `Authorization: Bearer` header by default so it never lands in proxy/access logs or `Referer` headers. Set `ACS_WHOISXML_KEY_IN_QUERY=1` to fall back to the legacy `?apiKey=...` query-string behavior on networks whose proxies strip Authorization headers. |
| `07-DomainRegistration.ps1` | ~405 | `Get-DomainRegistrationStatus` — orchestrates RDAP → WHOIS → API fallback chain, returns creation/expiry dates; expose raw RDAP data when available. If raw WHOIS/RDAP data is the only available content, show it inline without a Raw button; only show the Raw WHOIS/RDAP button when structured WHOIS/RDAP fields are also present and the raw content is hidden behind a collapsible section. When the only response is the IANA "This TLD has no whois server" referral (e.g. `.gr` / `.ελ` via FORTH), the raw banner is suppressed and the registry's web-form URL is exposed via the `registryWebForm` field so the SPA can render a friendly link panel. The TCP WHOIS provider (`Invoke-TcpWhoisLookup` in `02-WhoisProviders.ps1`) also explicitly rejects IANA's own TLD-level delegation record (matched by the combined presence of the `% IANA WHOIS server` header and a `source: IANA` field) via `Test-WhoisRawTextHasUsableData` so registries that publish no port-43 referral (e.g. FORTH for `.gr`) don't accidentally surface IANA's TLD record (`domain: GR`, `created: 1989-02-19`, ...) as if it were the queried domain's registration data — that would have caused the WHOIS card to show a misleading raw blob while the Email Quota row still correctly reported ERROR because no real fields parsed out. |

### Metrics & Configuration

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `03-MetricsHashKey.ps1` | ~117 | `$script:AppVersion` (currently `2.13.0`), metrics hash key persistence, `Get-HashedDomain`, `Handle-MetricsRequest` |
| `03a-SecureLogging.ps1` | ~370 | Privacy-safe structured logging: approved-field allowlist, random non-semantic correlation IDs, centralized redaction, safe exception summaries, stack-trace hashes, optional JSONL file sink (`ACS_LOG_FILE`) with size cap/rotation (`ACS_LOG_MAX_BYTES`), and configurable minimum level (`ACS_LOG_LEVEL`). Console rendering is human-first: `Write-AcsConsoleEvent` prints each already-sanitized event as one clean, colored (ANSI when the host supports it), single-line record (emitted with a single `Write-Host` so concurrent request runspaces cannot interleave), while the JSONL file sink stays compact JSON. `Test-AcsConsoleJsonMode` selects text vs JSON for the console — `ACS_LOG_CONSOLE=text|json` overrides, else text for interactive terminals and JSON when output is redirected/piped (`[Console]::IsOutputRedirected`), so containers/CI still get machine-readable logs. `Write-AcsStartupBanner` prints a prominent, clickable web URL banner at server start (text mode only; called from `24-RequestLoop.ps1` just before the accept loop so it is the LAST thing shown after all startup logs). The console line is built ONLY from the sanitized `$safe` event, so allowlist/redaction guarantees are preserved. `New-AcsCorrelationId` uses `RandomNumberGenerator.Create().GetBytes()` (portable across Windows PowerShell 5.1 / PowerShell 7) so correlation IDs are always random — the old static `RandomNumberGenerator.Fill()` is missing on .NET Framework 4.8 (5.1) and produced all-zero (`AAAA…`) IDs. `Write-AcsConsoleEvent` hides `correlationId` on Information-level console lines (it is kept for Warning/Error/Critical and is ALWAYS present in the JSON file sink) so routine request lines stay clean while still showing the request `method`/`route`/`statusCode`. `Test-AcsConsoleJsonMode` and `Write-AcsConsoleEvent` are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1` (both reachable from `Write-AcsLogEvent` on the request path) and the `AcsLogConsoleMode` value is shared into the runspace pool; `Write-AcsStartupBanner` is main-runspace only. Do not bypass this module with raw `Write-Information`, `Write-Warning`, `Write-Error`, `Write-Host`, or serialized objects in application runtime code. |
| `09-AnonymousMetrics.ps1` | ~361 | Optional anonymous usage metrics — persistence, aggregation counters, file I/O |
| `10-SessionCookies.ps1` | ~288 | Anonymous session tracking, session cookie management, `Update-AnonymousMetrics`. The `Secure` attribute on `acs_session` only honors the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header when the immediate TCP peer is in `ACS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (mirrors `Get-ClientIp`); otherwise it falls back to `Request.Url.Scheme` so an untrusted client cannot trick the server into stamping `Secure` on a plaintext cookie. |

### Utility Functions

| File | Lines | Contents |

| `05-DateUtilities.ps1` | ~145 | `ConvertTo-NullableUtcIso8601`, `Get-DomainAgeDays`, `Get-DomainAgeParts`, `Format-DomainAge`, `Get-TimeUntilParts`, `Format-ExpiryRemaining` |
| `06-DmarcGuidance.ps1` | ~85 | `Get-DmarcSecurityGuidance` — analyzes DMARC records and produces security recommendations |
| `11-HttpHelpers.ps1` | ~175 | HTTP response helpers: `Set-SecurityHeaders`, `Write-Json`, `Write-FileResponse`, `Write-Html`. The CSP in `Get-SecurityHeaderMap` must keep `frame-src 'self' https://login.microsoftonline.com`: MSAL's `ssoSilent()` and `acquireTokenSilent()` renew tokens via a hidden iframe to the Entra authorize endpoint, so dropping `frame-src` makes the browser fall back to `default-src 'self'`, block the iframe, and fail silent SSO with `redirect_bridge_timeout`. Framing headers are `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` (NOT `DENY`/`'none'`): Entra redirects MSAL's hidden iframe back to our own `redirectUri` (same origin), so the page must be allowed to frame itself; `SAMEORIGIN`/`'self'` still blocks all cross-origin clickjacking. The SPA also skips its full bootstrap when `window.self !== window.top` (running inside MSAL's hidden frame) and runs an MSAL-only init there. `connect-src` must likewise keep the Microsoft Graph / login / ARM / Log Analytics origins for the client-side auth + Azure flows. `Invoke-OutboundHttp` (the centralized outbound helper for DoH/RDAP/WHOIS/RBL) never lets `Invoke-WebRequest`/`Invoke-RestMethod` auto-follow redirects; it follows them **manually** one hop at a time (each hop uses `-MaximumRedirection 0`) and re-validates every redirect **target** with the website probe's public-IP guard (`Test-WebsiteHostIsPublic` from `16b-WebsiteProbe.ps1`) plus an https-only check before connecting, so a compromised upstream cannot 3xx-redirect an internal lookup to a private/metadata address (e.g. `169.254.169.254`). The initial operator-configured endpoint is intentionally exempt from the public-IP check so internal/split-horizon resolvers keep working; the common no-redirect path is byte-identical to a plain `Invoke-RestMethod` call, so DoH/RDAP/WHOIS deserialization and error propagation are unchanged. `Write-Html` takes a `-BaseUrl` and resolves the SEO tokens `__ACS_SITE_URL__` and `__ACS_ROBOTS__` **per request** (the SPA here-string is built once at startup and cannot know the public hostname). |
| `11a-SeoMetadata.ps1` | ~460 | SEO + AI-agent discovery. Serves `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/llms.txt` ([llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) Markdown brief), `/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1), `/favicon.svg` and `/og-image.svg` (both generated in memory by `Get-AcsBrandSvg` so the single-file distribution stays intact). `Get-AcsPublicBaseUrl` returns the public origin: `ACS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` wins, else it derives scheme+authority from the request, honoring `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-Host` **only** when the TCP peer passes `Test-IsTrustedProxy` (same trust model as `Get-ClientIp`). `Test-AcsSafeUrlAuthority` restricts the echoed authority to hostname/IPv6-literal charset + optional port so a spoofed `Host` cannot inject markup into `canonical`/`og:url`. Because a derived origin is client-influenced, `23-RequestHandler.ps1` serves `/robots.txt` + `/sitemap.xml` with `Cache-Control: no-store` unless `Test-AcsPublicBaseUrlIsConfigured` is true — otherwise one spoofed `Host` could poison a CDN copy for everyone. `robots.txt` explicitly names AI crawlers (`Get-AcsAiUserAgents`) and grants them `/api/*` too, because the tool answers factual DNS questions; `ACS_AI_DISALLOW=1` flips that block to `Disallow: /`, and `ACS_SEO_NOINDEX=1` disallows everything for everyone and switches the page `<meta name="robots">` to `noindex, nofollow`. **All 14 functions are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`**, and `AcsAppVersion` is shared into the pool as a session-state variable (reference it UNQUALIFIED — `$script:AppVersion` does not cross the runspace boundary). **PowerShell gotcha:** several helpers build JSON/XML with the `-f` operator, where a literal `{` or `}` MUST be doubled (`{{` / `}}`) or `[string]::Format` throws at runtime — this shipped broken once and surfaced as an HTTP 500 on `/openapi.json` only. |
| `12-DnsResolution.ps1` | ~194 | DNS resolution via DoH plus detailed DNS record collection, reverse-lookup supplements, related-name supplements (ACS DKIM selectors, `_dmarc.<domain>`, `www.<domain>`) so well-known subdomains surface in the records grid, TTL formatting helpers, readable decoding for escaped DNS labels, authoritative fallback collection for records like `HINFO` and `RRSIG`, a one-shot `Get-DohDnssecAnomaly` probe (without `cd=1`) so the SPA can surface a friendly informational note when an upstream DNSSEC validation failure (e.g. malformed TLD RRSIG) is silently being worked around, a one-shot `Get-DohResolutionStatus` probe (TXT-typed, **with** `cd=1` so it mirrors the real lookup path and is therefore NOT a DNSSEC failure) that returns `{ status, statusLabel, isServfail, summary }` only on **SERVFAIL** (Status 2) so the SPA can distinguish a broken/propagating authoritative zone from a genuine \"no record\" \u2014 this is what fixes the \"SPF resolves in MXToolbox but shows No Records here\" split-nameserver case (observed with a real-world domain), and a fast System-resolver-to-DoH fallback inside `ResolveSafely` and `Resolve-DnsRecordsDetailed` that short-circuits when the System resolver returns SERVFAIL/timeout (Win32 9002/9701) so single-name multi-type lookups don't pay the 15s timeout per type on broken zones such as during `.de` DNSSEC outages. NXDOMAIN/no-records (9003/9501) is preserved as a fast negative answer. Functions: `Resolve-DohName`, `ResolveSafely`, `Get-DnsIpString`, `Get-MxRecordObjects`, `Get-DohDnssecAnomaly`, `Get-DohResolutionStatus`, `Get-DnsRecordsStatus`. `Get-DohResolutionStatus` is registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`. `Get-DnsBaseStatus` (`16-DnsChecks.ps1`) runs it only when no SPF record is found (queried + parent) and exposes the result as `txtResolution`; `18-AggregatedDns.ps1` adds the SERVFAIL summary to guidance and suppresses the misleading \"SPF is missing\"/\"ACS TXT is missing\" advice in that case; the SPF card, TXT card, and Email-Quota SPF row in `20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1` render a SERVFAIL-specific WARN (keys `spfServfailDetected`/`txtServfailDetected`/`guidanceTxtServfail` in `20b`). |
| `13-InputValidation.ps1` | ~69 | `ConvertTo-NormalizedDomain`, `Test-DomainName` — domain input sanitization |
| `14-SpfAnalysis.ps1` (multiplicity + reachability) | — | Beyond the Outlook-include machinery documented below: `Select-SpfRecordFromSet` picks the analyzed record out of a duplicate set (prefers the one with the Outlook include so the ACS verdict does not depend on RRset ordering) and `Merge-SpfRecordSet` produces the ready-to-paste merged record; **both are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`**. `Get-SpfNestedAnalysis` applies the same RFC 7208 3.2/4.5 duplicate rule at **every include and redirect target** (>1 `v=spf1` at a target sets a PermError on that node instead of silently taking the first, which used to report a clean chain for a poisoned one). It also honors RFC 7208 6.1 — a `redirect=` is NOT expanded, NOT counted toward the 10-lookup limit, and gets `ignoredByAll = $true` when the record also has an `all` mechanism (pre-scanned before the token loop because `all` can appear *after* the redirect token); `Find-SpfOutlookRequirementMatch` skips such a subtree. RFC 7208 5.1 unreachable **mechanisms** after `all` are collected into `unreachableTerms`, excluded from the lookup count, and excluded from the Outlook match (`Test-SpfOutlookIncludeToken` breaks at a bare `all`) — **modifiers** (`exp=`, `redirect=`, vendor extensions) are deliberately exempt because RFC 7208 4.6.1 makes modifier position insignificant, and flagging them would fire on valid records. |
| `15-RequestUtilities.ps1` | ~324 | `Write-RequestLog`, `Get-RequestCorrelationId`, `Set-RequestCorrelationHeader`, `Get-ClientIp`, `Test-IsTrustedProxy`, `Get-ApiKeyFromRequest`, `Test-StringEqualsConstantTime`, `Test-ApiKey`, `Test-RateLimit`. `Write-RequestLog` emits only structured non-PII request events through `Write-AcsLogEvent`: the HTTP `method` and the `route` (the URL **path only** — e.g. `/api/mx`; the domain is always a query-string parameter, which is never read here) plus `statusCode` and a random correlation ID. It must never log domains, IPs, user agents, headers, query strings, bodies, or user-entered values. `Test-RateLimit` accepts a clamped `-Multiplier` so cheap, high-frequency endpoints (such as `/api/metrics`) can share the per-IP bucket with a more generous effective limit. The default per-IP cap is **240 req/min** (raised from 60) so a full multi-domain sweep (up to 10 domains × ~10 endpoints ≈ 100 requests) does not trip the shared bucket; override with `ACS_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`. `Test-ApiKey` uses `Test-StringEqualsConstantTime` to defeat timing-based key recovery. `Test-AcsClientDisconnect` classifies an exception as "the caller hung up" (walks the inner-exception chain for `HttpListenerException` / `SocketException`, or an `IOException` wrapping a `SocketException`). The outermost catch in `23-RequestHandler.ps1` uses it to log `REQ-CLIENT-DISCONNECTED` at **Debug** and skip the response write, instead of the old `ACS-REQ-500` **Error**: the SPA aborts in-flight fetches on every new lookup (`activeLookup.controllers`) and browsers drop connections on reload/navigation, so aborted requests are routine and previously spammed the console with ERROR lines for healthy behavior. |

### DNS Analysis

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
passes `Get-SpfOutlookRequirementStatus` returns `matchType = 'flattened-include'` with a detail string explaining that the upstream EOP ranges were detected inline. Canonical ranges are **never hard-coded** — they always come from the live `spf.protection.outlook.com` TXT record so the check stays correct as Microsoft updates its published ranges. A fifth path handles **macro-delegated** SPF: when the customer uses a hosted/dynamic SPF service that publishes a macro-based include (e.g. `include:%{i}._ip.%{h}._ehlo.%{d}._spf.vali.email`), the Outlook authorization is resolved per message from the live sending IP/HELO/MAIL FROM and cannot be statically confirmed or denied. After the flattening coverage check fails, `Find-SpfMacroDelegatedTarget` (raw-token scan first, then the expanded include/redirect nodes) detects the macro target and `Get-SpfMacroDelegationProvider` maps its suffix to a provider name (Valimail, OnDMARC, Sendmarc, EasyDMARC, dmarcian, Red Sift). `Get-SpfOutlookRequirementStatus` then returns `isPresent = $null`, `matchType = 'macro-delegated'`, plus `provider`/`macroTarget` fields and a provider-aware `error` string. This indeterminate verdict propagates through `16-DnsChecks.ps1` (`spfRequiredIncludeProvider`, `spfRequiredIncludeMacroTarget`), `18-AggregatedDns.ps1`, and the UI, where the SPF card and Email-Quota SPF row render **WARN** (not FAIL) and `getLocalizedSpfRequirementSummary`/`buildGuidance` show the `spfOutlookRequirementMacroDelegated[Provider]` translation telling the operator to verify Exchange Online is enabled in the provider console. New functions `Get-SpfMacroDelegationProvider` and `Find-SpfMacroDelegatedTarget` are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`. |
| `16-DnsChecks.ps1` | ~848 | Individual check endpoints: `Get-DnsBaseStatus`, `Get-DnsMxStatus`, `Get-DnsDmarcStatus`, `Get-DnsDkimStatus`, `Get-DnsCnameStatus`. **Record multiplicity is first-class here — do NOT reintroduce first-match-wins.** `Get-DnsBaseStatus` collects the FULL `v=spf1` set into `spfRecords` and reports `spfRecordCount` / `spfMultipleRecords`, because RFC 7208 3.2/4.5 makes more than one SPF record a **PermError** (SPF fails for every message; taking the first both hides the fault and judges the domain on an arbitrary record, since RRset order varies per resolver). `spfValue` stays a single record for back-compat but is chosen by `Select-SpfRecordFromSet` (14), which prefers the record carrying `include:spf.protection.outlook.com` so the ACS verdict is deterministic. `Merge-SpfRecordSet` (14) builds `spfMergedSuggestion`, a ready-to-paste single record (deduped terms, `redirect=` converted to `include:` because the merged record ends in `all`, and the MOST permissive `all` qualifier so merging can never silently tighten policy). `Get-DnsDmarcStatus` does the same for DMARC via the nested `Get-DmarcRecordSet`: RFC 7489 6.6.3 says a set with multiple qualifying records means receivers apply **no DMARC at all**, so it emits `dmarcRecords` / `dmarcRecordCount` / `dmarcMultipleRecords`. The duplicate count is taken over **strictly** qualified records (`^v\s*=\s*DMARC1\s*;`) only — the old loose `^v=dmarc` prefix would count junk TXT as a duplicate and raise a false alarm — with a fallback to a loosely-matched record for display so a malformed record still surfaces. `ms-domain-verification` yields `acsValues` (multiplicity is legal there, one per ACS resource/tenant, but readiness is presence-based so the operator needs to see all of them). DKIM selector lookups join `.Strings` **per record**: `$txtRecords.Strings -join ''` member-enumerates across the whole answer set and spliced two rotating keys into one value that exists in no record. |
All five functions are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`. The rendered `card-website` is captured by the existing full-page `screenshotPage`, so the snapshot appears in the exported PNG automatically. |
The four top-level functions are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`; the nested socket/parse helpers inside `Invoke-RawDnsTxtQuery` are not. The rendered `card-nameservers` (with its collapsible `toggleNameserverDetails` panel) is captured by `screenshotPage`. The `/api/nameservers` payload is ALSO consumed by `getDnsTxtRecoveryState` (`20c-HtmlJsUtilities.ps1`) as a **third TXT-recovery source**: when `/api/base` + `/api/records` return no queried-domain TXT (the public DoH resolver returned an empty answer for this lookup — typically a transient SERVFAIL/timeout from the authoritative DNS, OR genuinely out-of-sync nameservers), the union of TXT records across responding (NOERROR) nameservers backfills the SPF/ACS/TXT cards. Such records are flagged `recoveredFromNameservers` and render **WARN** (never PASS) with the `*RecoveredFromNameservers` notes, and `acsReady` is forced false (Azure verifies via public DNS), so the cards stop contradicting this card while still telling the operator the record is not resolving publicly. IMPORTANT: the recovery notes must NOT assert the nameservers are inconsistent — the Nameserver TXT Consistency card frequently reports `consistent` because the failure is an intermittent authoritative SERVFAIL (observed live with a real-world domain: ~1 in 4 Cloudflare DoH TXT lookups returned SERVFAIL while the nameservers served identical records), so the copy describes both possible causes and points at that card. |
| `17-DnsReputation.ps1` | ~430 | RBL/DNSBL reputation checking with caching: `Invoke-RblLookup`, `Get-DnsReputationStatus`. DNSBL zones are validated and bounded (`ACS_RBL_MAX_ZONES`), only public IPv4 targets are queried, target IP fan-out is bounded (`ACS_RBL_MAX_IPS`), parallelism is configurable (`ACS_RBL_MAX_PARALLELISM`), DNSBL policy-block replies are counted as errors instead of listings, positive listings attempt to include provider TXT reason text, and result ordering is stable for deterministic UI/API output. Nested helper functions inside `Get-DnsReputationStatus` do not need runspace registration. |
| `16d-DnsPropagation.ps1` | ~1,486 | Global DNS propagation check behind `/api/propagation`: `Get-DnsPropagationTypeCode`, `Get-DnsPropagationResolverCatalog`, `Get-DnsPropagationHealthTtlMinutes`, `Get-DnsPropagationHealthState`, `Set-DnsPropagationHealthState`, `ConvertFrom-DnsPropagationResolverInput`, `Select-DnsPropagationResolvers`, `Read-DnsNameFromBuffer`, `ConvertFrom-DnsPropagationRdata`, `New-DnsPropagationQueryPacket`, `Read-DnsPropagationResponse`, `Invoke-DnsPropagationTcpFanout`, `Invoke-DnsPropagationFanout`, `Get-DnsPropagationStatus` — **all fourteen are registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`** (none are nested, deliberately, so nothing races). Answers the complement of `16c`: not "do my nameservers agree?" but "can the rest of the world see the record yet?" Queries an inline catalog of **283 IPv4 resolvers across 80 countries** (30 curated majors + 253 community open resolvers generated from the public-dns.info dataset, cross-referenced with the standalone tool's vetted-healthy cache and live-probed before commit; each carries country/city/lat/lon/`anycast`/`region`, overridable via `ACS_PROPAGATION_RESOLVERS`). Regions are `global|namer|samer|europe|asia|africa|oceania`, plus `custom` for user-supplied addresses. **Resolver validation** replaces the standalone tool's background vetting job: asking for N builds a candidate pool of up to 3N (cap 300), queries the WHOLE pool in one fan-out with the REAL question, and keeps the first N that returned a usable answer — validating with the actual query (not a stand-in like `example.com`) is deliberate, because a resolver can answer a tiny A record and still fail a 60-record TXT set that needs TCP. Health is remembered in the process-wide TTL'd `$AcsPropagationHealth` ConcurrentDictionary (`ACS_PROPAGATION_HEALTH_TTL_MIN`, default 30) shared into the pool by `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1`; reference it UNQUALIFIED inside functions (like `$AcsRateLimitStore`) or workers see an empty variable. Net effect: asking for 100 returns 100 responding resolvers, and validation usually makes the check FASTER because dead servers stop holding the fan-out open. `ConvertFrom-DnsPropagationResolverInput` parses user-supplied resolvers (`ip`, `ip label`, or `ip|label`); it accepts public IPv4 literals ONLY — hostnames are refused so nothing is resolved on a user's behalf — and returns null lat/lon so custom entries are excluded from the map rollup instead of landing at 0,0. A `partial` (FAIL) verdict needs `norecord >= 5%` of responders once there are 20+ responders, so one ad-blocking resolver in a 100-server sample cannot flip a healthy domain to FAIL. **Concurrency:** deliberately NOT `[Parallel]::ForEach` (that runs PowerShell functions on multiple .NET threads sharing ONE runspace, which is not thread-safe). Instead one non-blocking UDP socket per resolver, all queries sent up front, then every socket awaited together with `[Socket]::Select` — genuinely concurrent at the network level, single-threaded in PowerShell, and ~one timeout window total regardless of resolver count. Queries set RD=1 (unlike `16c`, which uses RD=0 because it wants each authoritative server's own view) and advertise EDNS0 4096; `Invoke-DnsPropagationTcpFanout` recovers TC=1 answers using the same Select pattern. **CRITICAL when calling `Socket.Select`:** pass the `ArrayList`s through plain variables, never `$( if (...) { $list } else { $null } )` — the subexpression ENUMERATES the list and hands Select a fixed-size `object[]` copy, so Select cannot strip the not-ready sockets and the subsequent `Receive()` blocks forever. Verdict is **consensus-based** (most common non-empty answer set) so no expected value is required; an optional `-ExpectedValue` substring overrides it. States: `propagated` (PASS) / `partial` (FAIL — present at some vantage points, missing at others) / `mismatch` (WARN) / `norecord` (WARN) / `unknown` (WARN). A resolver only counts as **responding** when it answered NOERROR or NXDOMAIN; `unavailable` (no answer), `error` (SERVFAIL/REFUSED/...) and `truncated` (unreadable over UDP, TCP retry failed) are reported in `results[]` but **excluded from the verdict, from `respondedCount`, and from the `locations` map rollup** so a flaky public resolver can never fail a healthy domain. The SPA mirrors this: only `propagated`/`mismatch`/`norecord` rows are rendered as chips, markers and detail rows, with a single `propagationExcludedNote` footnote reporting how many were dropped. Env: `ACS_DISABLE_PROPAGATION_PROBE`, `ACS_PROPAGATION_MAX_RESOLVERS` (default 25, max 100), `ACS_PROPAGATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, `ACS_PROPAGATION_HEALTH_TTL_MIN`, `ACS_PROPAGATION_RESOLVERS`. **PowerShell 7.6 / .NET 10 gotcha:** a `List[object]` built with `New-Object` throws "Argument types do not match" when wrapped in `@( ... )`; this file uses `[System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()` and `.ToArray()` throughout. |
| `18-AggregatedDns.ps1` | ~171 | `Get-AcsDnsStatus` — aggregates all DNS check results into one response, including the DNS records table payload. Also propagates the duplicate-record verdicts (`spfRecords`/`spfMultipleRecords`/`spfMergedSuggestion`, `acsValues`, `dmarcRecords`/`dmarcMultipleRecords`) and adds the merge guidance. When picking a single value out of a possibly-array branch (e.g., `$effectiveSpfRecords`, `$effectiveAcsValues`), always wrap the **entire** `if/else` expression in `@(...)`: PowerShell unwraps a single-element array returned from an `if` expression back into a scalar, so the previous `if (...) { @(...) } else { @($base.spfValue) }` form silently collapsed to the raw SPF string and `[0]` then indexed the first character (`"v"` instead of the full `v=spf1 ...` record). Likewise wrap `$effectiveTxtRecords`, `$effectiveIpv4Addresses`, and `$effectiveIpv6Addresses` with `@(if ...)` so a 1-element collection survives as an array. |

### Embedded Web UI (SPA)

The web UI is split across seven files that build the `$htmlPage` here-string via concatenation (`$htmlPage = @'...'@` then `$htmlPage += @'...'@):

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `20-HtmlCss.ps1` | ~3,298 | Initializes `$htmlPage`. Contains `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<head>`, and all CSS styles through `</style>` |
| `20a-HtmlScriptSetup.ps1` | ~146 | External script tags (html2canvas CDN, MSAL loader), HTML `<body>` structure, main `<script>` tag opening with global JS variables. The MSAL loader uses a local-first source list (`/assets/msal-browser.min.js` first, then CDN fallbacks) and applies optional Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes from the `__ACS_MSAL_SRI__` template token (operator-supplied via `ACS_MSAL_SRI` env var as a JSON object: `{"<src>":"sha384-..."}`). The inline early-focus safety-net script under the search input is nonce-bound (`nonce="__CSP_NONCE__"`) so it executes under the strict CSP without `'unsafe-inline'`. |
| `20b-HtmlTranslations.ps1` | ~6,301 | All JavaScript i18n data: `TRANSLATIONS`, `TRANSLATION_EXTENSIONS`, `REMAINING_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES`, `MX_PROVIDER_HINTS`, `WHOIS_STATUS_LABELS`, `RISK_SUMMARY_LABELS`, `RUNTIME_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES`, `GUIDANCE_AND_AZURE_OVERRIDES`, `EXPLAINED_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES` (SPF/DMARC Explained tables, per-row Expansion Explain, CIDR info labels, prefix qualifiers, and mechanism/tag/value descriptions), language config constants. Latin-script languages (`es`, `fr`, `de`, `pt-BR`) ship the full 71-key set; non-Latin scripts (`ar`, `zh-CN`, `hi-IN`, `ja-JP`, `ru-RU`) ship the 25 user-visible UI labels (column headers, button labels, CIDR labels, empty/show/hide states) and let the longer descriptive sentences fall back to English via the existing `t()` chain. |
| `20c-HtmlJsUtilities.ps1` | ~2,123 | JavaScript utility functions: language switching, domain normalization/validation, cookie consent management, history management, HTML escaping, localization helpers, guidance text formatting, test summary. Also hosts the **DNS Propagation** client helpers: `propagationSettings` state + `normalizePropagationSettings`/`loadPropagationSettings`/`savePropagationSettings` (persisted under `acsPropagationSettings`, `functional` consent), `buildPropagationQuery()` (the extra query string appended to `/api/propagation` by both the initial lookup and the per-card re-check), the busy-state helper `setPropagationBusy()` (toggles `.is-busy` on `.prop-shell`, `.prop-map-wrap` and `.prop-details-block` immediately when a re-check starts; every builder re-applies it from `propagationRerunInFlight` so an unrelated re-render mid-flight cannot clear it, and `.prop-shell.is-busy` hides all values derived from the previous answer while the map stays under its spinner), and the dependency-free mini world map (`PROP_WORLD_SHAPES` coarse lon/lat rings, `propMapX`/`propMapY` equirectangular projection clipped to lat [-58, 84], `buildPropagationWorldPath`, `declutterPropagationMarkers`, `buildPropagationMapSvg`, `buildPropagationLegendHtml`). **No Leaflet / tile server / CDN** — the map is inline SVG styled by CSS classes so it follows the theme, keeps the CSP strict, and renders offline. `buildGuidance()` also emits the `guidancePropagation*` entries. |
highlights the dominant in-view section's link (`.section-rail-link-active`). The rail can be **collapsed** via a chevron button in its header (`toggleSectionRailCollapsed()`): when collapsed the rail gains `.section-rail-collapsed`, tucks flush to the left edge (`left:0`), and shows only a slim vertical "Jump to Section" tab (`.section-rail-expand`, a rotated label + arrow) to re-expand it. The collapsed state is persisted via `consentAwareSetItem`/`consentAwareGetItem` under the functional-category key `acsSectionRailCollapsed` (`SECTION_RAIL_COLLAPSED_KEY`) and re-applied on every render by `applySectionRailCollapsedState()`. For both navs every result card must expose a `card-...` id and a `<strong>` title — the Guidance (`card-guidance`), Helpful Links (`card-helpfulLinks`), and External Tools (`card-tools`) cards were given ids specifically so they appear. Translation keys: `jumpToSection`, `jumpToTag`, `jumpToSectionCollapse`, `jumpToSectionExpand`. CSS: `.section-nav-*` and `.section-rail-*` in `20-HtmlCss.ps1`. |
| `20e-HtmlAzureIntegration.ps1` | ~924 | Azure/MSAL authentication, ARM API calls, subscription/resource/workspace discovery, Log Analytics query execution, closing `</script></body></html>` |
| `20f-HtmlPostProcess.ps1` | ~22 | PowerShell template replacements: injects `__APP_VERSION__`, `__ENTRA_CLIENT_ID__`, `__ENTRA_TENANT_ID__`, `__ACS_API_KEY__`, `__ACS_ISSUE_URL__`, and `__ACS_MSAL_SRI__`. Every value substituted into a JS string literal is run through `ConvertTo-JsStringLiteralBody` to escape `\`, `'`, `"`, control characters, and angle brackets so a hostile env var can never break out of the literal or close the surrounding `<script>` block. `__ACS_MSAL_SRI__` is round-tripped through `ConvertFrom-Json`/`ConvertTo-Json` and falls back to the literal `null` on malformed input. |

## Encoding & i18n Notes

- All non-ASCII characters in JavaScript translation strings use `\uXXXX` Unicode escape sequences to prevent encoding corruption on non-UTF-8 locales.
- The `looksLikeMojibake()` function in `20c-HtmlJsUtilities.ps1` uses precise regex requiring continuation-byte chars (U+0080–U+00BF) after lead-byte chars to avoid corrupting valid accented characters (Portuguese, French, Spanish).
- Supported languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Arabic (RTL), Portuguese (Brazil), Chinese (Simplified), Hindi, Japanese, Russian.

## Tips for Copilot / Contributors

1. **Never edit `acs-domain-checker.ps1` directly** — edit `src/` files and run `Build-Release.ps1 -Force`.
2. **Adding a new source file?** Name it with the appropriate number prefix to control load order (e.g., `16a-NewFeature.ps1` loads after `16-DnsChecks.ps1`).
3. **Translations live in `20b-HtmlTranslations.ps1`** — this is the largest file (~3,400 lines) because it contains all 10 language translations.
4. **CSS is in `20-HtmlCss.ps1`** — all styling for the web UI.
5. **The JavaScript `render()` function** is in `20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1` — this is the main function that builds the results UI after a domain lookup.
6. **API endpoint routing** is in `23-RequestHandler.ps1` — look here to understand which URL path maps to which handler.
7. **DNS check logic** for each record type is in `16-DnsChecks.ps1`.
Active highlight classes are `.spf-record-token-active`, `.spf-explained-row-active`, and `.spf-expansion-row-active`; preserve these names if the CSS is refactored. **CIDR info button**: ip4/ip6 rows in the SPF Explained table render a small `.spf-cidr-info-btn` "i" button beside the value that is **click-to-expand** (not hover); clicking it toggles a hidden sibling `<tr class="spf-cidr-detail-row">` placed directly under the same row, which renders the Network/CIDR prefix/Subnet mask/Range/Size breakdown inside `<pre class="spf-cidr-detail-pre">` (monospace + `white-space: pre`) so the padded labels stay column-aligned. Parsing lives in `parseSpfIpv4` / `parseSpfIpv6` (both use BigInt mask math so `/0` and `/128` survive), formatting lives in `formatSpfCidrInfo`, and the toggle is `toggleSpfCidrDetail(element, detailId)` in `20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1`. The button gets a `.spf-cidr-info-btn--open` class while expanded so CSS can visually indicate the open state. Unique detail-row ids are minted from the module-level `__spfCidrDetailCounter` so multiple SPF Explained panels on the page (the queried-domain panel plus every per-row Expansion Explain panel) never collide. The labels are translation keys (`spfCidrLabelNetwork`, `spfCidrLabelPrefix`, `spfCidrLabelMask`, `spfCidrLabelRange`, `spfCidrLabelSize`, `spfCidrLabelAddresses`, `spfCidrRangeThrough`); locales without overrides fall back to English via `t()`.
9. **If you add a new PowerShell function that can be called during HTTP request handling**, also add it to the `$functionNames` list in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1` so it is imported into the runspace pool. **This is a required step** — server-side functions execute inside worker runspaces that only have the functions registered in `$functionNames`; calling an unregistered (non-nested) function from a request path throws "command not recognized" and surfaces to the user as an **HTTP 500 Internal Server Error** for that specific check (e.g. the Domain Registration / WHOIS row). Note that **nested** functions (defined inside another function's body) and the TcpListener-shim helpers in `24-RequestLoop.ps1` that run only in the main runspace do **not** need registration. After adding or removing any server-side function, run the registration audit and confirm it reports `PASS`:

   ```powershell
   pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./tools/Audit-RunspaceFunctions.ps1
   ```

   `tools/Audit-RunspaceFunctions.ps1` statically walks the call graph from the request-handler entry point (`$handlerScript` in `23-RequestHandler.ps1`), computes the transitive closure of reachable server-side functions, and diffs it against `$functionNames`. It correctly ignores nested functions and strips comments/strings to avoid false positives. Treat any "MISSING REGISTRATIONS" output as a build blocker.
9a. **Secure logging validation is mandatory for logging/diagnostics changes.** Runtime application logging must go through `Write-AcsLogEvent` / `Write-AcsLogException` only. Do not log domains, IP addresses, headers, query strings, request/response bodies, user-entered text, local paths, environment variables, raw exception messages, raw stack traces, tokens, cookies, API keys, tenant/subscription/account/customer identifiers, or serialized objects. Correlation IDs must come from `New-AcsCorrelationId` and must never be derived from request data. After changing logging, exception handling, request handling, startup/shutdown diagnostics, or log configuration, run:

   ```powershell
   pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./tools/Test-SecureLogging.ps1
   ```

   Treat any prohibited-pattern failure as a security blocker.
10. If substantial changes are done, increment the version number. For example, if it was version 1.0.1, increment to 1.0.2. If the changes are breaking, increment to 1.1.0, and if it's a major change, increment to 2.0.0. This is important for metrics and for users to understand the level of change in each release. When the version is updated, also update the version shown in GitHub workflows and in `README.md`, and keep Copilot instructions in sync. Note that `README.md` also contains **example** version strings (the `git tag v<version>` / `git push origin v<version>` release steps, the `docker pull ...:<version>` / `linux-<version>` / `windows-<version>` examples, the workflow-dispatch version example, and `acs-domain-checker-dockerhub.ps1 -Version <version>`) — bump those to the new version too so the docs never reference a stale release.
11. If there are any substantial changes to the application, please update this document to reflect the new structure or logic! This is meant to be a living document that evolves with the codebase. With it being so large, it needs a guide to navigate effectively.
12. In the DNS records table UI, ensure the Name and Type columns do not wrap; keep them single-line and rely on horizontal scrolling for readability. The Type column header and values should always stay on one line and not wrap. TTL values should show raw seconds plus a compact abbreviated duration such as `5d 2h 33s` when applicable, omitting zero-value units like `0m` and `0s` unless needed for a zero-duration value. The DNS records table should remain searchable/filterable, support toggling yellow row highlighting for screenshot-ready troubleshooting, and use a removable filter-chip workflow beneath the search box for clearer multi-filter behavior. Enum-style `Class` and `Type` filtering should continue to use exact-match dropdown suggestions with keyboard navigation. Default ordering should be `Type`, then `Name`, then `Data`, with a post-sort step that splices CNAME->TXT chains together so a resolved TXT record (e.g., a DKIM public key on the CNAME target) is rendered immediately under the CNAME row that points at it (`reorderDnsCnameTxtChains` in `20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1`). Because the Name/Type columns are `nowrap`, the whole table can exceed its card width, so it is wrapped in a `.dns-records-table-wrap` (`overflow-x: auto`) container that scrolls horizontally INSIDE the card at any viewport width. The `.dns-record-data` (DATA) cell has a `min-width: 340px` floor: without it the auto table layout squeezes the breakable DATA content down to a few px and wraps even a short timestamp one character per line ("unreadable"); the floor forces the table wider than the card so the scroll container engages instead. DATA / detail values use `overflow-wrap: anywhere; word-break: normal` so long base64 (DNSKEY/RRSIG) still breaks when needed but ordinary text (dates) never breaks mid-token.
13. When routes, API behavior, configuration, or other user-facing functionality changes, update `README.md` in the same change so repository documentation stays current. Additionally, maintain Copilot instructions to keep documentation in sync.
14. Local UI assets such as toolbar/status SVG icons and language flag SVGs can be downloaded with `Download-UiAssets.ps1`. Keep that script in sync with the asset names referenced by `20b-HtmlTranslations.ps1` and `20c-HtmlJsUtilities.ps1`.
15. Make sure any code changes performed have sufficient comments surround it so its easy to understand the intent and logic when coming back to it later, especially for complex sections like the SPF recursive expansion or the HTTP request handling logic. This will help both human readers and Copilot understand the code better in the future.
16. When exposing raw RDAP data in the domain registration UI, prefer a digestible grouped presentation (status, events, nameservers, contacts, links, then expandable raw JSON) rather than showing only an undifferentiated JSON blob, favor polished summary/timeline/card layouts over plain bullet lists when possible, and order RDAP events chronologically. In the Guidance section, avoid surfacing terminal DNS TXT timeout guidance until the lookup workflow has settled, and suppress that specific message when the detailed DNS records payload already confirms TXT records were collected. Likewise, TXT-dependent checks/cards and the Domain card address view should recover from the detailed DNS records payload when the dedicated base lookup data is incomplete but queried-domain DNS records are still available there.
17. **Screenshot capture (`screenshotPage` in `20c-HtmlJsUtilities.ps1`)**: the page is rendered at `html { zoom: 1.1 }` (in `20-HtmlCss.ps1`), but html2canvas 1.4.1 does **not** support the CSS `zoom` property — it measures boxes with zoom applied but paints glyphs un-zoomed, which garbles dense monospace content (e.g. base64 DKIM keys). The capture therefore resets `clonedDoc.documentElement.style.zoom = "1"` in the `onclone` hook and compensates with `scale = devicePixelRatio * pageZoom` so the output stays crisp. If you change the page zoom or upgrade html2canvas, re-validate the screenshot output. The Clipboard API write can reject (lost focus during the multi-second render, or a non-secure `http://` origin); `screenshotPage` re-focuses the window and **falls back to downloading the PNG** (`screenshotDownloadedFallback` translation) instead of dead-ending, so only require `window.html2canvas` up front, not the Clipboard API.
18. **Multi-domain lookups (`20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1`, `20a`, `20-HtmlCss.ps1`, `20b`)**: the address box accepts several space/comma/semicolon-separated domains, each committed as a removable chip (`#domainChips`, `.domain-chip` with an X in the corner). State lives in `multiDomainState = { domains, results, active, running }` and `domainChipTokens` (declared in `20b` near `activeLookup`). Entry point is `runLookupFromInput()` (wired to the Lookup button and the Enter keyup); it collects `getEnteredDomains()` (chips + trailing input, normalized/validated/deduped, capped at `MAX_LOOKUP_DOMAINS = 10`) and calls `runMultiDomainLookup(domains)`. Lookups run **sequentially** (one domain fully completes before the next) so the single shared `#results` container, the per-run `activeLookup` cancellation, and the server's per-IP rate limiter are never overwhelmed. **Key architectural constraint:** result-card element IDs are global, so only ONE domain is ever in `#results` at a time — `render(r)` computes fully for every domain (always storing `r._quotaCopyBase` and `multiDomainState.results[r.domain]`) but only *paints* `#results` / the status line / the section rail when `r.domain === multiDomainState.active` (the `paintResult` gate). `lookup()` takes `options.fromMulti` (skip the single-domain `resetMultiDomainState` + skip writing `input.value`/title so the box stays chip-only) and `options.skipUrlUpdate` (the sweep sets a single space-joined `?domain=` URL). Tabs (`#domainTabs`) are built by `updateDomainTabsUI()` and are shown whenever **≥1** domain has been checked (so the current domain is always labeled, even for a single lookup); the bar is `position: sticky; top: 0` so it follows the top of the page while scrolling through results. IMPORTANT: for that sticky to work, `<body>` uses `overflow-x: clip` (NOT `hidden`) — `hidden` makes the body a scroll container and silently breaks `position: sticky`, while `clip` still suppresses horizontal overflow. `showDomainTab(d)` re-renders the cached result (or a `domainCheckQueued` placeholder). `buildQuotaCopyPayload()` stacks every domain's `_quotaCopyBase` table (separated by a divider) with the shared intake block appended once. Bootstrap: `parseDomainListParam()` + `applyDomainsToInputBox()` make `initializePage`/`scheduleInitialLookup` multi-aware. Intake `getAllIntakeSendingDomains()` feeds `maybeRunCheckerForIntakeDomain()` so **all** listed sending domains are checked. New UI strings (`removeDomainLabel`, `domainCheckQueued`, `checkingMultipleDomains`) live in `MULTI_DOMAIN_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES` (`20b`, all 10 languages).
19. **Customer Intake form i18n (`20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1`)**: the intake questionnaire is localized via the `INTAKE_LOCALES` data table (keyed by language code; non-ASCII `\uXXXX`-escaped per repo convention). Each locale supplies section headers, per-field canonical question text (which doubles as both the inserted template line AND a primary extraction pattern so the two never drift), clarifier strings, and the replace-confirm prompt. `buildIntakeTemplateHtml(lang)` renders the localized **Insert template** output (mirrors the English `INTAKE_TEMPLATE_HTML` structure, `escapeHtml`-guarded, falls back to English for `en`/unsupported); `prefillIntakeForm()` calls it with `currentLanguage`. Extraction is **additive**: the `augmentIntakeExtractionForLocales()` IIFE merges every locale's question text into the matching `INTAKE_EXTRACT_FIELDS[].patterns` and builds `INTAKE_LOCALIZED_SECTION_HEADERS` (consumed by `isIntakeSectionHeader`) + `INTAKE_LOCALIZED_MARKERS` (appended to the `normalizeIntakePlainText` split markers, longest-first) — the English matching is never weakened. `parseIntakeNumeric` normalizes Arabic-Indic/Eastern Arabic-Indic/Devanagari/full-width digits to ASCII so localized numeric answers still drive throttling-tier inference. The extracted-field **labels** and the **Copy Email Quota** payload deliberately stay English (the canonical ACS questionnaire); only the inserted editor template and the recognized question phrasings are localized — the form does NOT machine-translate the customer's answer values. The extracted **Type of emails sent**, **Current tier level**, and **Expected tier level** rows use English dropdown suggestion values from `INTAKE_FIELD_OPTIONS` / `INTAKE_TIERS` only when empty, but the cell stays editable so custom text is always allowed; tier rows expose an `intake-tier-info-btn` that toggles the `buildIntakeTierTableHtml()` reference table. To add/adjust a language, edit `INTAKE_LOCALES` (author UTF-8 then `\u`-escape) and rebuild; no extractor changes are needed because the augmentation is data-driven.

20. **DNS Propagation card (`20d-HtmlJsCore.ps1`, `20c`, `20-HtmlCss.ps1`, `20b`)**: the `card-propagation` render block sits between the Nameserver and CNAME cards. It is the one card with its own **settings** UI: a gear button (`.prop-settings-btn`) in `titleSuffixHtml` toggles `#propagationSettingsPanel` (built by `buildPropagationSettingsHtml(prop)`, whose location checkboxes come from the server's `availableRegions` so the picker always mirrors the live catalog). Because `render()` rebuilds the entire results list on every partial result, the open/closed state of the settings and details panels lives in the module-level `propagationSettingsOpen` / `propagationDetailsOpen` flags, NOT in the DOM — otherwise the panel would slam shut mid-edit whenever a slower check finished. `applyPropagationSettings()` reads the form, normalizes + persists it, and calls `rerunPropagationCheck()`, which re-fetches **only** `/api/propagation` (never the other nine endpoints) for `getActivePropagationResult()` — the result object for `multiDomainState.active`, not necessarily `lastResult`. `fetchJson(path, extraQuery)` gained a second parameter so the `requests` entry `{ key: 'propagation', path: '/api/propagation', query: buildPropagationQuery }` can append the settings on the initial lookup. Badge mapping: `propagated`=PASS, `partial`=FAIL, everything else=WARN; the Table of Contents and section rail pick this up automatically because both derive from the card's `.tag` class. Translation keys live in `PROPAGATION_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES` (`20b`; full sets for en/es/fr/de/pt-BR, short UI labels for the non-Latin scripts). CSS is the `.prop-*` block in `20-HtmlCss.ps1`; the card body is rich HTML so the plain-text summary needs the explicit `.prop-summary-text` (`white-space: pre-wrap`) wrapper.

21. **SEO / AI-agent metadata (`11a-SeoMetadata.ps1`, `20-HtmlCss.ps1` head, `20a`, `21`, `20f`)**: the `<head>` in `20-HtmlCss.ps1` carries description, robots, canonical, 11 `hreflang` alternates, Open Graph + Twitter card tags, and a `WebApplication` JSON-LD block (nonce-bound so it survives the strict CSP). Two tokens are resolved **per request** by `Write-Html`: `__ACS_SITE_URL__` (from `Get-AcsPublicBaseUrl`) and `__ACS_ROBOTS__` (from `Test-AcsSeoIndexingAllowed`); `__ACS_OG_IMAGE__` is resolved once at startup in `20f-HtmlPostProcess.ps1` and, unlike every other token there, lands in an **HTML attribute** rather than a JS string literal — so it uses HTML-attribute escaping, NOT `ConvertTo-JsStringLiteralBody` (which would emit literal `\u003C` sequences into the markup). A non-`http(s)` `ACS_OG_IMAGE` is rejected and falls back to the built-in card. `20a-HtmlScriptSetup.ps1` adds a `<noscript>` block so crawlers/agents that do not run JS see a real description instead of the toolbar button labels (that was the original symptom: Google rendered the snippet as "Dark mode Copy link Copy page screenshot..."). When adding a page or locale, update `Get-AcsSeoLanguages`, the `hreflang` links in the head, and `Get-AcsSitemapXml` together. The visible `<title>` and the `pageTitle` translation key are deliberately left in sync — change both or neither, because `updateTitle()` in `20c` overwrites `document.title` from `t('pageTitle')` on every render. **After touching SEO metadata, template tokens, the language list, or any `/api/*` route, run the validator and confirm it reports `PASS`:**

    ```powershell
    pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./tools/Test-SeoMetadata.ps1
    ```

    `tools/Test-SeoMetadata.ps1` statically checks (a) the language list is identical across `LANGUAGE_OPTIONS`, `Get-AcsSeoLanguages` and the `hreflang` links, (b) every `__TOKEN__` in the HTML templates has a `.Replace()` site so it cannot ship literally into the page, (c) every `-f` format string in `11a` actually formats (the doubled-brace trap above), (d) every served lookup endpoint is documented in BOTH `/llms.txt` and `/openapi.json`, and (e) the required `<head>` tags exist and the JSON-LD block still carries its CSP nonce. It is mutation-tested: all six of those invariants were deliberately broken and each was detected.

22. **`tools/Audit-RunspaceFunctions.ps1` here-string handling**: the brace matcher used to leave here-string mode on the `'@` terminator but then re-read that same `'` as the start of a NEW single-quoted string, swallowing the following braces and reporting any function containing a here-string as "REGISTERED BUT NOT DEFINED". It now skips past the whole terminator (and uses `[ \t]*`, not `\s*`, so a blank line cannot match a later terminator early). If you see that warning for a function you can clearly see defined, verify with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` before assuming the registration is wrong.

23. **Crawler `HEAD` requests and hidden-tab bootstrap**: every response writer (`Write-Json`, `Write-FileResponse`, `Write-Html`, `Write-TextResponse`) must call `Test-AcsHeadRequest` before writing bytes to an `HttpListenerResponse`; writing a body for `HEAD` throws `ProtocolViolationException` and turns every crawler probe into HTTP 500. The TcpListener shim accepts `HEAD`, sets `_suppressBody`, emits the same `Content-Length` it would for GET, and sends no body bytes. `scheduleInitialLookup()` keeps its two-frame foreground animation path but also calls the idempotent `startInitialLookup` through a 250 ms timer, because browsers can pause `requestAnimationFrame` indefinitely for a `?domain=` page opened in a background tab. Both invariants are checked by `tools/Test-SeoMetadata.ps1`.

24. **DNS record multiplicity is a first-class concern — never collapse an RRset to a single value.** A real customer domain (`soma-q.com`) published three `v=spf1` records; the SPF card showed only the first and rendered FAIL for the Outlook include while the DNS records table on the same page listed all three. Rules that follow from that:
    - **Server:** collect the whole set (`spfRecords`, `acsValues`, `dmarcRecords`, DKIM `TxtValues`) and report a count + a `*MultipleRecords` flag. Keep the legacy scalar for back-compat, but derive it deterministically (`Select-SpfRecordFromSet`), never from RRset order.
    - **RFC verdicts:** >1 SPF record = PermError (RFC 7208 3.2/4.5) ⇒ hard FAIL. >1 qualifying DMARC record = no policy applied at all (RFC 7489 6.6.3) ⇒ FAIL on the card, WARN in the quota row. Multiple `ms-domain-verification` records are **legal** (one per ACS resource) ⇒ show them all, no badge change. Multiple DKIM TXT at one selector is **legal** (RFC 6376 3.6.2.2) ⇒ show them all; the bug there was `$records.Strings -join ''` member-enumerating across the set and fabricating a key.
    - **Duplicate detection must be strict.** Count only records that strictly qualify (`^v\s*=\s*DMARC1\s*;`), or junk TXT produces false alarms. This was the single change the adversarial review forced.
    - **SPA:** `getDnsTxtRecoveryState` returns `spfRecords`/`spfMultipleRecords`/`acsValues`; `render()` paints every record, leads the card with the PermError note, and appends the `spfMergedSuggestion`. Keys live in `RECORD_MULTIPLICITY_TRANSLATION_OVERRIDES` (`20b`).
    - **Do NOT add** void-lookup-limit tracking or unknown-mechanism PermError detection. Both were evaluated and rejected: static expansion cannot distinguish NXDOMAIN from a transient resolver failure, and `Get-SpfMechanismType` cannot distinguish an unknown mechanism from a valid modifier, so both would warn on healthy domains.

25. **Multi-`<character-string>` TXT must go through `ConvertFrom-DnsTxtPresentationData` (`12-DnsResolution.ps1`).** DoH returns TXT RDATA in presentation form as space-separated quoted strings (`"partA" "partB"`); RFC 1035 3.3.14 allows 255 octets per string and RFC 7208 3.3 requires concatenating with NO separator. Stripping only the OUTER quotes leaves the inner `" "` embedded, which corrupts every record over 255 octets — most visibly a 2048-bit DKIM key rendering as `...50v8r" "RRo9toe...` in the records grid. That walker was originally inline in `Resolve-DohName` only; `Resolve-DohRecordsDetailed` had the naive version, so the `/api/records` grid was corrupt on any DoH-only host (including the shipped Linux image, which has no `Resolve-DnsName`). It is now one shared helper registered in `22-RunspaceSetup.ps1` — use it on any new TXT-reading path rather than re-implementing quote stripping.

26. **A verdict must never contradict data shown on the same page.** Recurring failure mode in this codebase, so check it when touching any card:
    - The Reputation card colors on `listed > 0` first, not on percentage: 1 listing across 25 zones still scores 96%, which used to paint a green `tag-pass` badge directly above its own `Listed: 1` body line while the Email-Quota row correctly said WARN.
    - Indeterminate is not failure. `spfHasRequiredInclude === null` (macro-delegated / hosted SPF) is WARN everywhere — the card, the checklist row, `getDomainQuotaStatus`, the tab dot and the copied summary must agree. They did not, and the aggregate reported FAIL for data the card called WARN.
    - `buildGuidance()` gates absence advice on `loaded.X && !errors.X`. A failed fetch sets **both**, so gating on `loaded` alone told operators to add MX/DMARC/DKIM/CNAME records the tool never managed to read.
